a: The minimum exchange rate against the euro
The National Bank's negative interest rate
62314.e: With the automatic exchange of information (AEOI), Switzerland has been sending account data of foreign clients to their countries of residence since 2018. The data have been collected since 2017.
62314.m: The automatic exchange of information makes foreign accounts visible to tax authorities.

62315.q: Which business area of Zurich's financial centre is associated with the company Swiss Re?
62315.e: Swiss Re, based in Zurich, is one of the largest reinsurers in the world. Reinsurers in turn insure insurance companies against large losses.
62315.m: Swiss Re insures insurers and is a reinsurer.

62316.q: In which area is Switzerland regarded as a world-leading location?
62316.e: Switzerland manages more assets for clients from abroad than any other country. Zurich and Geneva are the most important locations for this.
62316.m: Switzerland is a world leader in cross-border wealth management.

62317.q: What does the term “too big to fail” mean in Swiss banking?
a: Systemically important banks whose collapse would endanger the economy
Banks that may not lend to foreigners
Banks that only operate in Switzerland
62317.e: Systemically important banks are so large and interconnected that their collapse would damage the whole economy. Stricter capital requirements apply to them in Switzerland.
62317.m: Systemically important banks must hold more capital because their collapse would be dangerous.

62318.q: Which two companies merged in 1996 to form the pharmaceutical group Novartis?
62318.e: In 1996 the Basel companies Ciba-Geigy and Sandoz joined to form Novartis. At the time it was one of the largest company mergers in the world.
62318.m: Novartis was formed in 1996 from Ciba-Geigy and Sandoz.

62319.q: Which generics manufacturer was spun off from Novartis and listed on the stock exchange in 2023?
62319.e: In October 2023 Novartis separated from its generics division Sandoz, which has been an independent company since then. Generics are cheaper copies of medicines whose patents have expired.
62319.m: Since 2023 Sandoz has been an independent company again.

62320.q: Which location factor particularly favoured the chemical industry settling in Basel?
a: The Rhine as a source of water and a transport route
Large coal deposits in the region
62320.e: The Rhine supplied water for production and was a transport route. Basel also lay on the border with Germany and France, which made exchange easier.
62320.m: The Rhine made Basel an ideal location for chemicals.

62321.q: Which Basel group built the tallest building in Switzerland with “Building 2”?
62321.e: The Roche tower “Building 2” is about 205 metres high and was completed in 2022. It replaced Roche's neighbouring “Building 1” as the tallest building in Switzerland.
62321.m: The Roche towers shape Basel's skyline.

62322.q: Which fire at a chemical company badly polluted the Rhine in 1986?
62322.e: On 1 November 1986 a Sandoz warehouse burned at Schweizerhalle near Basel. Toxic chemicals got into the Rhine with the firefighting water and killed large numbers of fish.
62322.m: The Schweizerhalle fire of 1986 caused a large fish kill in the Rhine.

62323.q: Which authority in Switzerland is responsible for approving medicines?
62323.e: Swissmedic is the Swiss Agency for Therapeutic Products, based in Bern. It examines and approves medicines before they may be sold.
62323.m: Swissmedic decides which medicines are approved in Switzerland.

62324.q: Which Basel agrochemical group was taken over by the Chinese state-owned company ChemChina in 2017?
62324.e: Syngenta makes pesticides and seeds and is based in Basel. The takeover by ChemChina was completed in 2017.
62324.m: Syngenta has belonged to a Chinese group since 2017.

62325.q: Besides medicines, which area is Roche's second main business?
62325.e: Roche consists of the Pharma and Diagnostics divisions. Diagnostics makes, for example, laboratory tests and measuring devices for hospitals.
62325.m: Roche works in pharmaceuticals and diagnostics.

62326.q: What is the cross-border life sciences network on the Upper Rhine around Basel called?
62326.e: BioValley links companies and universities from Switzerland, Germany and France. Basel is the centre of this trinational cluster.
62326.m: In BioValley, companies from three countries work together in life sciences.

62327.q: Which religious rule encouraged watchmaking in Geneva in the 16th century?
62327.e: The reformer John Calvin banned the wearing of jewellery in Geneva. Many goldsmiths therefore turned to making watches.
62327.m: Calvin's jewellery ban steered Geneva's goldsmiths towards watchmaking.

62328.q: With which neighbouring country did Switzerland have watchmaking craftsmanship added to the UNESCO intangible cultural heritage list in 2020?
62328.e: Switzerland and France submitted the joint nomination “Craftsmanship of mechanical watchmaking and art mechanics”. The Jura Arc stretches across both countries.
62328.m: Watchmaking craftsmanship in the Jura Arc has been UNESCO intangible cultural heritage since 2020.

62329.q: Which technical innovation triggered a severe crisis in the Swiss watch industry in the 1970s?
62329.e: Cheap quartz watches, mainly from Japan and the USA, pushed out mechanical Swiss watches. Tens of thousands of jobs in the Jura Arc were lost.
62329.m: The quartz crisis cost the Swiss watch industry many jobs.

62330.q: Which product contributed greatly to the recovery of the Swiss watch industry from 1983?
62330.e: The Swatch was a cheap, mass-produced plastic quartz watch with few parts. It helped the industry win back market share.
62330.m: The Swatch helped the Swiss watch industry out of the crisis.

62331.q: Which body tests the accuracy of mechanical watch movements and awards the chronometer certificate?
62331.e: The official Swiss chronometer testing institute COSC tests movements for several days in different positions and temperatures. Only accurate movements may be called chronometers.
62331.m: Only watches tested by COSC may be called chronometers.

62332.q: What was the early production system called in which farming families in the Jura made watch parts at home?
62332.e: In établissage, an entrepreneur (établisseur) shared out the making of the individual parts among many home workers. The parts were then assembled into a watch in one place.
62332.m: In établissage, many home workers made watch parts.

62333.q: Why was watchmaking particularly suitable as a second source of income for farmers in the Jura?
a: Long winters left plenty of time for work at home
There were rich gold mines in the Jura
The farmers were not allowed to keep animals
62333.e: In the harsh climate of the Jura, field work stopped during the long winter. The farming families used this time to make watch parts in their living rooms.
62333.m: Long winters made watchmaking a second income for Jura farmers.

62334.q: In which town does the Federation of the Swiss Watch Industry (FH) have its seat?
62334.e: The Fédération de l'industrie horlogère suisse (FH) has its seat in Biel/Bienne. Biel is also the headquarters of large watch groups.
62334.m: Biel is a centre of the Swiss watch industry.

62335.q: Which valley in the Vaud Jura is known for watches with especially complicated movements?
62335.e: In the Vallée de Joux, with places such as Le Brassus and Le Sentier, watches with complications such as moon phases or minute repeaters have long been made. The valley is regarded as the cradle of haute horlogerie (fine watchmaking).
62335.m: The Vallée de Joux is famous for complicated watch movements.

62336.q: In which municipality in Zug does the commodities group Glencore have its headquarters?
62336.e: Glencore, one of the largest commodities groups in the world, has its headquarters in Baar in the canton of Zug. The canton of Zug is an important location for international commodity trading.
62336.m: Glencore has its headquarters in Baar in the canton of Zug.

62337.q: Which trader founded the company in Zug in 1974 that later became Glencore?
62337.e: The commodity trader Marc Rich founded Marc Rich + Co AG in Zug in 1974. After he left, the company was renamed Glencore in 1994.
62337.m: With his company, Marc Rich laid the foundation for Glencore.

62338.q: Which city is Switzerland's most important centre for trading oil and grain?
62338.e: Large commodity traders such as Vitol, Trafigura, Gunvor and Mercuria have offices or their headquarters in Geneva. Oil, grain and oilseeds in particular are traded there.
62338.m: Geneva is a world centre for oil and grain trading.

62339.q: What is meant by merchanting (transit trade)?
a: Goods are bought and sold without ever entering Switzerland
Goods are transported through Switzerland on the Rhine
Goods are processed in Switzerland and exported again
Goods are only traded within Switzerland
62339.e: In merchanting, a Swiss company buys commodities abroad and sells them to customers abroad. The goods themselves never cross the Swiss border.
62339.m: In merchanting the goods never touch Switzerland.

62340.q: Which popular initiative on corporate liability won a majority of the people in 2020 but failed to win a majority of the cantons?
62340.e: The Responsible Business Initiative received about 50.7 per cent yes votes on 29 November 2020. Because most cantons rejected it, it was still not accepted.
62340.m: The Responsible Business Initiative failed in 2020 because of the majority of the cantons.

62341.q: Which location advantage drew many commodity traders to the canton of Zug?
a: Large ore deposits in the canton
A port on Lake Zug for ocean-going ships
62341.e: As early as the 1940s, the canton of Zug lowered taxes for holding and domiciliary companies. This attracted many international trading firms.
62341.m: Low taxes made Zug attractive for commodity traders.

62342.q: Which industry association represents commodity trading and shipping firms in Switzerland?
62342.e: The Swiss Trading and Shipping Association (STSA), based in Geneva, represents commodity traders, trade finance banks and shipping companies. It grew out of a Geneva association.
62342.m: The STSA represents Switzerland's commodity trading industry.

62343.q: Which banking service is especially important for commodity trading in Geneva?
62343.e: Commodity traders need short-term loans and guarantees to pay for large cargoes before they are sold on. Specialised banks in Geneva offer this trade finance.
62343.m: Without trade finance, commodity traders could hardly pay for large cargoes.

62344.q: Why is a landlocked country like Switzerland still a centre of commodity trading?
a: Trading is done with contracts, not with goods in the country
All the world's commodities are transported on the Rhine
Switzerland has the largest warehouses in Europe
62344.e: Commodity trading mainly involves organising contracts, financing and logistics. So what matters is experts, banks, legal certainty and taxes, not physical access to the sea.
62344.m: Commodity trading needs expertise and financing, not necessarily a port.

62345.q: In car-free Zermatt, how are guests and goods mainly transported within the village?
62345.e: No ordinary cars with combustion engines may drive in Zermatt. Small electric vehicles run in the village, and guests arrive by train.
62345.m: Zermatt is a car-free resort with electric vehicles.

62346.q: Where do most guests park their cars before taking the shuttle train to Zermatt?
62346.e: For guests, the road into the Matter Valley ends in Täsch. From there a shuttle train of the Matterhorn Gotthard Railway takes a few minutes to Zermatt.
62346.m: From Täsch guests take the train to Zermatt.

62347.q: Who led the first ascent of the Matterhorn in 1865?
62347.e: The Englishman Edward Whymper reached the summit with his rope team on 14 July 1865. On the way down, four men fell to their deaths.
62347.m: Edward Whymper was the first to climb the Matterhorn, in 1865.

62348.q: Which railway has run from Zermatt to over 3,000 metres since 1898?
62348.e: The Gornergrat Railway opened in 1898 and was the first electric rack railway in Switzerland. The top station is at about 3,089 metres.
62348.m: The Gornergrat Railway has run electrically up the Gornergrat since 1898.

62349.q: Which mountain station near Zermatt is the highest cable car station in Europe?
62349.e: The Matterhorn Glacier Paradise station on the Klein Matterhorn is at about 3,883 metres. It is the highest station in Europe that can be reached by cable car.
62349.m: Matterhorn Glacier Paradise is Europe's highest cable car station.

62350.q: Why can you also ski near Zermatt in summer?
a: Because of the glacier ski area on the Theodul Glacier
Because of indoor ski halls in the village
Because it always snows there in summer
Because of plastic slopes in the valley
62350.e: On the Theodul Glacier near the Klein Matterhorn there is enough snow for slopes even in summer. This makes Zermatt one of the few year-round ski areas in the Alps.
62350.m: Thanks to the glacier, you can ski near Zermatt all year.

62351.q: Which epidemic hit Zermatt in 1963 and damaged its reputation as a holiday resort?
62351.e: In 1963 more than 400 people in Zermatt fell ill with typhoid because contaminated drinking water was used. Afterwards the water supply was greatly improved.
62351.m: A typhoid epidemic forced Zermatt to improve its water supply in 1963.

62352.q: Which hotelier shaped Zermatt's rise as a holiday resort in the 19th century?
62352.e: Alexander Seiler took over a first inn in Zermatt in 1854 and then built several hotels. His family shaped tourism in the village for generations.
62352.m: Alexander Seiler was one of the pioneers of tourism in Zermatt.

62353.q: Since 2023, where does the Matterhorn Alpine Crossing cable car link lead from Zermatt?
62353.e: Since 2023 the Matterhorn Alpine Crossing has linked Zermatt with Breuil-Cervinia via the Klein Matterhorn and Testa Grigia. This lets you cross the Alps by cable car.
62353.m: Since 2023 a cable car link has run from Zermatt to Cervinia.

62354.q: Which condition must farms meet to receive direct payments?
62354.e: Direct payments are only made if a farm provides proof of ecological performance (PEP). This includes, for example, a balanced fertiliser budget, crop rotation and areas for biodiversity.
62354.m: Without proof of ecological performance there are no direct payments.

62355.q: Roughly how much money does the Confederation pay out in direct payments every year?
62355.e: Direct payments make up the largest part of the Confederation's spending on agriculture. For years they have amounted to about 2.8 billion francs a year.
62355.m: The Confederation pays farmers about 2.8 billion francs in direct payments every year.

62356.q: Unlike earlier price and sales guarantees, what is the aim of direct payments?
a: To pay for services to the public and the environment regardless of how much is produced
To produce as much milk as possible
To raise prices in the shops
62356.e: In the past the state guaranteed prices and purchases, which led to overproduction. Direct payments, by contrast, pay for services to the community such as landscape care and biodiversity.
62356.m: Direct payments reward services to the public instead of large quantities.

62357.q: As a rule, what percentage of its agricultural land must a farm set aside as biodiversity promotion areas?
62357.e: For proof of ecological performance, as a rule 7 per cent of the land must be biodiversity promotion areas, such as extensive meadows or hedges. A lower share applies to special crops.
62357.m: As a rule at least 7 per cent of the land serves biodiversity.

62358.q: Among other things, which tasks does the Federal Constitution give Swiss agriculture?
a: Supplying the population and caring for the cultivated landscape
Running the ski areas in the Alps
Training the army in the mountains
62358.e: Article 104 of the Federal Constitution, accepted by the people in 1996, names among other things supplying the population and caring for the cultivated landscape. It allows the Confederation to pay for such services with direct payments.
62358.m: The Federal Constitution also obliges agriculture to care for the landscape.

62359.q: Which type of payment encourages animals to be let outdoors regularly?
62359.e: RAUS stands for “regular outdoor exercise” in German and is one of the animal welfare payments. Farms receive money if their animals regularly go out to pasture or into an outdoor run.
62359.m: RAUS payments reward farmers whose animals regularly go outdoors.

62360.q: Which federal office is responsible for paying out direct payments?
62360.e: The Federal Office for Agriculture (FOAG) implements agricultural policy and regulates direct payments. They are paid to the farms via the cantons.
62360.m: The Federal Office for Agriculture is responsible for direct payments.

62361.q: What do mountain farmers receive extra slope payments for?
62361.e: Steep meadows are hard to mow and need more work. With slope payments, part of the cultivated landscape payments, the Confederation wants to prevent such land from becoming overgrown.
62361.m: Slope payments help keep steep meadows open.

62362.q: Which type of payment supports the care of regional landscapes according to cantonal projects?
62362.e: Landscape quality payments were introduced with the agricultural policy 2014 to 2017. They promote, for example, traditional standard fruit orchards, dry stone walls or varied crops in regional projects.
62362.m: Landscape quality payments promote beautiful and varied cultivated landscapes.

62363.q: What is using the alpine pastures with livestock during the summer months called?
62363.e: During summer grazing, cows, cattle, sheep and goats spend the summer on alpine pastures. This relieves the valley farms, and fodder in the valley can be harvested for the winter.
62363.m: During summer grazing, livestock graze on the alp in summer.

62364.q: Which Valais cattle breed is known for its cow fights when the herds go up to the alp?
62364.e: When going up to the alp, Hérens cows naturally fight to decide the pecking order in the herd. This led to the Valais cow fights, in which a queen is crowned.
62364.m: Hérens cows decide the queen of the alp by fighting.

62365.q: Which unit does Switzerland use to measure the stocking of an alp with livestock?
62365.e: One normal stocking unit is equal to summer grazing one livestock unit for 100 days. It helps to avoid overgrazing the alps.
62365.m: The normal stocking unit measures how much livestock an alp can support.

62366.q: What is farming on several levels called, in which the livestock climb higher and higher over the summer?
62366.e: In tiered farming, the livestock move from the valley farm via spring pastures (Maiensässe) to the high alp and back in autumn. In this way the fodder at different altitudes is used one after the other.
62366.m: In tiered farming, the livestock follow the grass growth upwards.

62367.q: What is an intermediate level between the valley farm and the high alp, used in spring and autumn, called?
62367.e: A Maiensäss lies between the valley and the alp and is used mainly in May and in autumn. The name comes from the month (Mai, May) in which the livestock move there.
62367.m: The Maiensäss is the intermediate level on the way to the alp.

62368.q: What is the person called who traditionally turns the milk into cheese on an alp?
62368.e: The Senn or Sennerin milks the cows and makes cheese and butter in the alpine hut. Alpine cheese, for example, is made this way.
62368.m: The Senn makes cheese from milk on the alp.

62369.q: Which Vaud alpine cheese with a protected designation of origin may only be made over an open wood fire?
62369.e: L'Etivaz AOP comes from alps in the Pays-d'Enhaut in Vaud. The milk is heated in a copper cauldron over an open wood fire.
62369.m: L'Etivaz is made on the alp over a wood fire.

62370.q: Why does alpine farming contribute greatly to preserving the mountain landscape?
a: Grazing stops alpine pastures from becoming overgrown with bushes
The livestock build roads on the alp
62370.e: Without grazing, many alpine areas would become covered in bushes and slowly overgrown by forest. Farming them keeps the pastures open and rich in species.
62370.m: Alpine pastures stay open because livestock graze them.

62371.q: Which form of organisation is common for alps in Switzerland when several farmers use an alp together?
a: Public limited company listed on the stock exchange
62371.e: Many alps belong to co-operatives, corporations or municipalities. The members share grazing rights and do communal work to maintain them.
62371.m: In alpine co-operatives, farmers use an alp together.

62372.q: Which country was the most important single buyer of Swiss exports in 2024?
62372.e: Measured by individual countries, the USA was Switzerland's most important export destination in 2024, ahead of Germany. The EU as a whole, however, remains the most important trading partner.
62372.m: The USA is Switzerland's largest single export market (as of 2024).

62373.q: Which economic area is overall Switzerland's most important trading partner?
62373.e: Switzerland conducts most of its trade in goods with the European Union. Relations are governed by bilateral agreements.
62373.m: The EU is Switzerland's most important trading partner.

62374.q: Which free trade organisation has Switzerland belonged to since it was founded in 1960?
62374.e: Switzerland was a founding member of the European Free Trade Association (EFTA) in 1960. Through EFTA it has concluded many free trade agreements.
62374.m: Switzerland has been a member of EFTA since 1960.

62375.q: With which large country did a bilateral free trade agreement with Switzerland come into force in 2014?
62375.e: The free trade agreement between Switzerland and China came into force on 1 July 2014. Switzerland was one of the first European countries with such an agreement.
62375.m: Since 2014 a free trade agreement has applied between Switzerland and China.

62376.q: What problem arises for exporters when the franc rises strongly in value?
a: Swiss products become more expensive abroad
62376.e: With a strong franc, foreign customers have to pay more of their own currency for Swiss goods. Exporting companies therefore lose competitiveness or profit margin.
62376.m: A strong franc makes Swiss exports more expensive abroad.

62377.q: When did the Swiss National Bank remove the minimum exchange rate of 1.20 francs per euro?
62377.e: The SNB introduced the minimum exchange rate in September 2011 to weaken the franc. On 15 January 2015 it surprisingly removed it, after which the franc rose sharply.
62377.m: The minimum euro exchange rate was removed in January 2015.

62378.q: Which organisation promotes the exports of Swiss SMEs on behalf of the Confederation?
62378.e: Switzerland Global Enterprise (S-GE) advises small and medium-sized enterprises on moving into foreign markets. It works on behalf of the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs.
62378.m: Switzerland Global Enterprise helps SMEs to export.

62379.q: Which 1992 vote result still shapes Swiss foreign economic policy today?
a: The rejection of joining the EEA
The acceptance of joining the EU
62379.e: On 6 December 1992 the people and the cantons narrowly rejected joining the European Economic Area. After that, Switzerland chose the bilateral path with the EU.
62379.m: After the no to the EEA in 1992, Switzerland relied on bilateral agreements.

62380.q: Besides pharmaceutical products, which export goods cause very high and strongly fluctuating Swiss export values in some years?
62380.e: A large part of the world's gold is refined in Switzerland, for example in Ticino. Gold exports fluctuate strongly and are often shown separately in statistics.
62380.m: Gold is refined in Switzerland and exported in large quantities.

62381.q: Why are there big differences in the tax burden between the cantons in Switzerland?
a: The cantons set their own tax rates
The Confederation sets random rates for each canton
Only large cantons may levy taxes
The municipalities pay taxes to the Confederation
62381.e: In Swiss federalism, cantons and municipalities have their own power to tax. They can set tax rates and so compete for companies and residents.
62381.m: Cantons set their own tax rates and compete with each other.

62382.q: Which federal act harmonises the principles of cantonal taxes without setting the tax rates?
62382.e: The Tax Harmonisation Act (StHG) regulates, for example, which income is taxed and how procedures work. The level of the tax rates remains a matter for the cantons.
62382.m: The Tax Harmonisation Act aligns the rules but not the rates.

62383.q: Which system has balanced out the differences in financial capacity between the cantons since 2008?
62383.e: With the new fiscal equalisation (NFA), financially strong cantons such as Zug and the Confederation pay to financially weak cantons. This softens the effects of tax competition.
62383.m: Fiscal equalisation shifts money from strong to weak cantons.

62384.q: Which canton pays the most per person into resource equalisation?
62384.e: Thanks to many companies and wealthy residents, Zug has the highest resource potential per person. That is why the canton pays the highest contributions per inhabitant to fiscal equalisation.
62384.m: Per person, Zug is the biggest payer in fiscal equalisation.

62385.q: Which proposal accepted in 2019 abolished the tax privileges for holding and domiciliary companies?
62385.e: The people accepted TRAF on 19 May 2019, and it came into force in 2020. It replaced special rules criticised internationally with new tools such as the patent box and brought extra money for the AHV.
62385.m: With TRAF the tax privileges for holding companies were abolished.

62386.q: Which minimum tax rate for large international groups did Swiss voters accept in 2023?
62386.e: On 18 June 2023 the people approved the implementation of the OECD minimum tax. Large groups with a turnover of over 750 million euros are to pay at least 15 per cent tax on profits.
62386.m: Under the OECD rule, large groups must pay at least 15 per cent tax on profits.

62387.q: What is the taxation of rich foreigners in Switzerland who do not work, based on their living costs, called?
62387.e: In lump-sum taxation (taxation according to expenditure), it is not income but living expenses that are taxed. Some cantons such as Zurich have abolished it.
62387.m: In lump-sum taxation, living expenses count instead of income.

62388.q: Which part of income tax is regulated in the same way for everyone in Switzerland, whatever their canton of residence?
62388.e: Direct federal tax is levied throughout Switzerland at the same rate. Differences only arise with cantonal and municipal taxes.
62388.m: Direct federal tax is the same in all cantons.

62389.q: What does a municipality's tax multiplier describe?
a: A percentage of the basic tax that the municipality sets every year
The height of the town hall
62389.e: Many cantons calculate a basic tax according to a fixed rate. The canton and municipalities levy a percentage of it, the tax multiplier, and can thus adjust their tax burden.
62389.m: With the tax multiplier, a municipality decides how high its taxes are.

62390.q: Which canton is regarded as the centre of the so-called Crypto Valley?
62390.e: Since about 2014 many blockchain and crypto firms have settled in the canton of Zug. That is why the region is called Crypto Valley.
62390.m: Crypto Valley is in the canton of Zug.

62391.q: Which well-known foundation behind a large blockchain platform was founded in Zug in 2014?
62391.e: The Ethereum Foundation was founded in Zug in 2014 and supports the development of the Ethereum blockchain. Its founding is seen as the starting point of Crypto Valley.
62391.m: The Ethereum Foundation made Zug a crypto centre.

62392.q: What did the city of Zug introduce in 2016 as one of the first authorities in the world?
62392.e: From July 2016 you could pay smaller administrative fees in the city of Zug with Bitcoin. This was an early example worldwide of an authority accepting cryptocurrency.
62392.m: Zug accepted Bitcoin for fees as early as 2016.

62393.q: Which federal act adapted Swiss law to blockchain technology in 2021?
62393.e: The Federal Act on the Adaptation of Federal Law to Developments in Distributed Ledger Technology (DLT) came into force in 2021. Among other things, it created ledger-based securities.
62393.m: With the DLT Act, blockchain got a legal basis in 2021.

62394.q: What does the abbreviation DLT stand for in connection with blockchain?
62394.e: DLT means Distributed Ledger Technology, a technology for shared electronic registers. A blockchain is the best-known form of it.
62394.m: A blockchain is a distributed electronic ledger.

62395.q: Which Swiss authority published guidelines on how to classify ICOs in 2018?
62395.e: In February 2018 FINMA set out how it classifies initial coin offerings (ICOs) and tokens legally. This created legal certainty for crypto firms in Crypto Valley.
62395.m: In 2018 FINMA created clarity for ICOs and tokens.

62396.q: What is an initial coin offering (ICO)?
a: Raising money by issuing digital tokens
The stock market listing of a big bank
62396.e: In an ICO, a project sells digital tokens, usually for cryptocurrencies, to raise money. Many Zug blockchain projects financed themselves this way around 2017.
62396.m: In an ICO a project raises money by selling tokens.

62397.q: Which association has represented the interests of blockchain firms in the Zug region since 2017?
62397.e: The Crypto Valley Association was founded in Zug in 2017. It connects companies, research and authorities in the field of blockchain.
62397.m: The Crypto Valley Association connects the blockchain scene in Zug.

62398.q: Which factors made Zug particularly attractive for blockchain firms?
a: Low taxes, open-minded authorities and closeness to Zurich's financial centre
Large data centres under Lake Zug
A ban on banks in the canton
62398.e: Zug offers low taxes and a business-friendly administration, and it is close to Zurich. In addition, the authorities were open to new technologies early on.
62398.m: Low taxes and open-minded authorities drew crypto firms to Zug.

62399.q: What is the name of the association of the Swiss mechanical, electrical and metal industries?
62399.e: Swissmem represents the MEM industries, which include mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, metalworking and precision instruments. The sector is one of the largest industrial employers in Switzerland.
62399.m: Swissmem represents the mechanical, electrical and metal industries.

62400.q: Which Jura town is regarded as the centre of décolletage, the making of small turned parts?
62400.e: In Moutier, the making of tiny turned parts and the building of automatic lathes developed out of the watch industry. These parts are also used today for medicine and cars.
62400.m: Moutier is known for décolletage and automatic lathes.

62401.q: From which industry did the precision industry in the Jura Arc mainly develop?
62401.e: The know-how for making tiny, precise parts comes from watchmaking. Many firms in the Jura now use it for medical technology, electronics and mechanical engineering.
62401.m: The precision industry in the Jura grew out of watchmaking.

62402.q: Which industry in Switzerland makes, for example, dental implants, hearing aids and pacemaker components?
62402.e: Medical technology (medtech) is a growing branch of the precision industry. It combines precision engineering skills with research and strict quality standards.
62402.m: Medical technology uses Swiss precision for medical products.

62403.q: Which research centre for microtechnology and electronics was founded in Neuchâtel in 1984?
62403.e: The Centre Suisse d'Electronique et de Microtechnique (CSEM) was founded in Neuchâtel in 1984. It brings research in microtechnology and electronics into industry.
62403.m: CSEM in Neuchâtel does research for microtechnology.

62404.q: Which apprenticeship is typical of the Swiss precision industry?
62404.e: Polymechanics make and machine precise parts on machine tools. The dual vocational education system is regarded as an important factor in the success of Swiss industry.
62404.m: Polymechanics are among the most important skilled workers in the precision industry.

62405.q: Which machine was originally developed for the Swiss watch industry and is now known worldwide as the “Swiss-type” lathe?
62405.e: In the sliding headstock lathe, the workpiece is pushed through a guide bush, which allows very precise long and thin parts. It was developed in Switzerland in the 19th century for making small watch parts.
62405.m: The sliding headstock lathe comes from the Swiss watch industry.

62406.q: Which location factor is particularly important for the high wages in the Swiss precision industry?
a: High value creation through quality and specialisation
62406.e: Swiss precision firms do not compete on low prices but on quality, innovation and niche products. This high value creation allows high wages despite the strong franc.
62406.m: Swiss precision firms rely on quality rather than quantity.

62407.q: Which university in Lausanne is an important partner of the precision and microtechnology industry in western Switzerland?
62407.e: The Swiss Federal Institute of Technology in Lausanne (EPFL) runs a large microengineering institute and has a site in Neuchâtel. Many firms work with it.
62407.m: EPFL works closely with microtechnology in western Switzerland.

62408.q: What share of Switzerland's electricity production came from hydropower in 2024?
62408.e: According to the electricity statistics of the Swiss Federal Office of Energy, about 60 per cent of national production came from hydropower stations in 2024. This makes hydropower by far the country's most important source of electricity.
62408.m: Hydropower supplies about three fifths of Swiss electricity.

62409.q: How much electricity did Switzerland produce in total in 2024 (national production)?
62409.e: National production in 2024 was about 80.5 terawatt hours. Because it was a wet year, Switzerland exported a net 14 TWh or so more electricity than it imported.
62409.m: Switzerland produced about 80 terawatt hours of electricity in 2024.

62410.q: Which canton produces the most electricity from hydropower?
62410.e: With its high peaks, glaciers and large reservoirs such as Lac des Dix, Valais has the largest hydropower production in Switzerland. With over 10 billion kilowatt hours a year, it supplies about 28 per cent of Swiss hydropower electricity.
62410.m: Valais is Switzerland's largest hydropower canton.

62411.q: What is the fee called that operators of hydropower stations pay the cantons and municipalities for using the water?
62411.e: The water rate is a payment for the right to use the water power of a river or lake. For many mountain cantons and municipalities it is an important source of income.
62411.m: Power stations pay a water rate for using hydropower.

62412.q: Which type of power station uses the constant flow of a river and can hardly store any water?
62412.e: Run-of-river power stations are on rivers such as the Rhine or the Aare and continuously produce electricity from the water flowing past. They supply baseload energy but can hardly shift production in time.
62412.m: Run-of-river power stations use the water that is flowing in the river at the moment.

62413.q: Why are storage power stations in the Alps particularly important for the electricity supply in winter?
a: They store meltwater from summer for winter
Most rain falls in the Alps in winter
They need no water in winter
They only run when rivers are frozen
62413.e: In summer, melting snow and glaciers fill the reservoirs. In winter, when consumption is high and inflow is low, the stored water can be sent through the turbines as needed.
62413.m: Reservoirs shift summer water into the electricity-hungry winter.

62414.q: With storage power stations, what is meant by hydropeaking (surge and low flow)?
a: Strong, short-term changes in flow in the river below the outlet
Waves on the reservoir during a föhn storm
Temperature differences between the surface and the bottom
62414.e: When a storage power station runs its turbines at times of high demand, the flow in the river suddenly rises (surge) and then falls again (low flow). This harms fish and small creatures, which is why the Water Protection Act requires remedial measures.
62414.m: Hydropeaking means artificial changes in flow below power stations.

62415.q: Which type of turbine is typically used for very large heads of water in alpine high-pressure power stations?
62415.e: In a Pelton turbine, a fast jet of water from a nozzle hits cup-shaped buckets. It is suitable for large heads and comparatively small amounts of water.
62415.m: Pelton turbines make especially good use of large heads of water.

62416.q: Which type of turbine is particularly suitable for river power stations with a low head and a large amount of water?
62416.e: The Kaplan turbine looks like a ship's propeller with adjustable blades. It works efficiently with low heads and large flows, as found on the Rhine and the Aare.
62416.m: Kaplan turbines are the specialists for river power stations.

62417.q: Which federal act requires a minimum amount of water to remain in the river below a water intake?
62417.e: The Water Protection Act regulates the so-called residual flows. They make sure that streams and rivers below power stations do not dry up and remain a habitat.
62417.m: Residual water protects life in streams below power stations.

62418.q: In which canton are the Linth-Limmern power stations?
62418.e: The facilities are in the upper Linth valley above Linthal. The host canton holds 15 per cent of the operating company.
62418.m: The Linth-Limmern power stations are in the canton of Glarus.

62419.q: What is the pumping and turbine output of the Limmern pumped storage power station?
62419.e: Four machine sets of 250 megawatts each give a total of 1,000 megawatts, both in pumping and in turbine mode. That is roughly the output of a large nuclear power station.
62419.m: The Limmern pumped storage power station produces about 1,000 megawatts.

62420.q: Which reservoir serves as the lower basin of the Limmern pumped storage power station?
62420.e: Water is pumped from Lake Limmern over 600 metres up into Lake Mutt and sent back down when needed. Lake Limmern holds about 92 million cubic metres.
62420.m: Lake Limmern is the lower basin of the Limmern pumped storage power station.

62421.q: How long is the dam of the upper reservoir of the Limmern pumped storage power station, inaugurated in 2016?
62421.e: The gravity dam at Lake Mutt is 1,054 metres long and lies at about 2,500 m above sea level. It is regarded as the longest dam in Switzerland.
62421.m: The Lake Mutt dam is over a kilometre long.

62422.q: Roughly how much did the “Linthal 2015” expansion with the new pumped storage power station cost?
62422.e: The investment for the Linthal 2015 project was about 2.1 billion francs. It is one of the largest construction projects in Swiss hydropower.
62422.m: The Linthal 2015 expansion cost over two billion francs.

62423.q: Where are the four machine sets of the Limmern pumped storage power station?
a: In a cavern about 600 metres deep inside the mountain
In a building on the dam
On a platform in the reservoir
62423.e: The machine hall was dug out as a cavern about 600 metres deep in the rock. This protects the facilities from avalanches and weather and spares the landscape.
62423.m: The machines of the Limmern pumped storage power station are in a rock cavern.

62424.q: When does a pumped storage power station typically pump water into the upper basin?
a: When there is surplus electricity and low prices
At peak consumption in the evening
Only in winter when it is freezing
62424.e: Pumped storage power stations use cheap surplus electricity, for example from solar or baseload energy, to pump water up. When demand is high, the water is sent through the turbines and the electricity is sold at a higher price.
62424.m: A pumped storage power station works like a giant battery made of water.

62425.q: What overall efficiency is typical of modern pumped storage power stations?
62425.e: When pumping and generating, losses occur in pumps, generators, pipes and through friction. About three quarters to four fifths of the energy used comes back.
62425.m: Pumped storage power stations give back about three quarters of the pumping energy.

62426.q: Roughly how much potential energy is there in 1,000 m³ of water falling 600 metres (g equals 9.81 m/s²)?
62426.e: 1,000 m³ of water has a mass of 1,000,000 kg. E is m times g times h, so 1,000,000 times 9.81 times 600 equals 5.886 billion joules; divided by 3.6 million that gives about 1,635 kWh, or roughly 1.6 MWh.
62426.m: Potential energy is calculated as mass times gravitational acceleration times height.

62427.q: Which energy company holds the majority of the Linth-Limmern power stations?
62427.e: Kraftwerke Linth-Limmern AG is a subsidiary of Axpo Power, which holds 85 per cent. The other 15 per cent belong to the host canton.
62427.m: The Linth-Limmern power stations belong mainly to Axpo.

62428.q: In which municipality is the Gösgen nuclear power station?
62428.e: The Gösgen nuclear power station stands on the Aare in the Solothurn municipality of Däniken. That is why the operating company is called Kernkraftwerk Gösgen-Däniken AG.
62428.m: The Gösgen nuclear power station is in Däniken in the canton of Solothurn.

62429.q: Which type of reactor is in operation at the Gösgen nuclear power station?
62429.e: Gösgen has a pressurised water reactor from the German company Kraftwerk Union. In the primary circuit the water is under such high pressure that it does not boil; the steam for the turbine is only produced in a separate circuit.
62429.m: In a pressurised water reactor the water in the reactor circuit stays liquid.

62430.q: In which year did the Gösgen nuclear power station start commercial operation?
62430.e: After trial operation, Gösgen went into commercial operation in autumn 1979. It produces about 8 billion kilowatt hours a year.

62431.q: Which type of reactor is in operation at the Leibstadt nuclear power station?
62431.e: Leibstadt has a General Electric BWR-6 boiling water reactor. Here the water turns to steam directly in the reactor pressure vessel and drives the turbine.
62431.m: In a boiling water reactor the steam is produced directly in the reactor.

62432.q: Which is the most powerful nuclear power station in Switzerland?
62432.e: After several increases in output, Leibstadt has a gross electrical output of about 1,285 megawatts. It covers about a sixth of Switzerland's electricity needs.
62432.m: Leibstadt is the most powerful nuclear power station in Switzerland.

62556.q: A train on a half-hourly timetable leaves at 7:14. When does the next train on this line leave?
62556.e: Half-hourly means a train leaves every 30 minutes. 7:14 plus 30 minutes is 7:44.
62556.m: On a half-hourly timetable, a train leaves every 30 minutes.

62560.q: A train on an hourly timetable leaves on the hour and takes 47 minutes to reach the next hub. How long do travellers wait there until the next full hour?
62560.e: The train arrives 47 minutes after leaving. Until the next full hour there are 60 minus 47 = 13 minutes left.
62560.m: If the journey time does not fit the timetable rhythm, there are waiting times at the hub.

62561.q: How many departures per hour in each direction does a suburban train line running every quarter of an hour have?
62561.e: An hour has 60 minutes. 60 ÷ 15 = 4, so a train leaves every 15 minutes.
62561.m: With a train every quarter of an hour, four trains run per hour.

62636.q: In which Lower Engadine village is the picture book story of “Schellen-Ursli” (A Bell for Ursli) set?
62636.e: Selina Chönz and Alois Carigiet set their 1945 story in the village of Guarda with its typical Engadine houses.

62637.q: Which region has the Vereina Tunnel connected with the Lower Engadine since 1999?
62637.e: The Vereina line of the Rhaetian Railway runs from Klosters in the Prättigau to Sagliains in the Lower Engadine.
62637.m: The Vereina Tunnel connects the Prättigau with the Lower Engadine.

62638.q: What is special about Samedan airfield in the Upper Engadine?
62638.e: Samedan airfield lies at around 1,700 m, making it the highest airfield in Europe.
62638.m: Samedan has the highest airfield in Europe.

62639.q: Which is the largest of the Upper Engadine lakes by area?
62639.e: At about 4 km², Lake Sils is larger than Lake Silvaplana, Lake Champfèr and Lake St. Moritz.
62639.m: Lake Sils is the largest lake in the Upper Engadine.

62640.q: Which spring custom is celebrated in the Engadine on 1 March with bells?
62640.e: At Chalandamarz, children walk through the village with cowbells to drive away the winter.
62640.m: At Chalandamarz, Engadine children ring in the spring.

62641.q: Which technique is used to decorate the façades of many Engadine houses?
62641.e: In sgraffito, a light layer of lime is placed over darker plaster and then scratched away to create patterns.
62641.m: Engadine houses often have scratched sgraffito patterns.

62642.q: What causes the holes in Emmental cheese?
a: Carbon dioxide from propionic acid bacteria
62642.e: Propionic acid bacteria break down lactic acid and produce carbon dioxide. The gas collects to form the typical holes.
62642.m: The holes in Emmental cheese come from gas made by bacteria.

62643.q: Which traditional team sport, in which a “Nouss” is struck, is very popular in the Emmental?
62643.e: In Hornussen, a player hits the Nouss with a long flexible stick, and the opponents try to stop it with wooden boards.
62643.m: Hornussen is a typical sport in the Emmental.

62644.q: Which natural event of 1837 did Jeremias Gotthelf describe in a story of its own?
a: a flood of the river Emme
62644.e: In “Die Wassernot im Emmental” (The Flood in the Emmental), Gotthelf describes the devastating storm of August 1837.
62644.m: Gotthelf wrote about the flood in the Emmental.

62645.q: Which mountain rises to around 1,400 m on the border between the Emmental and the Entlebuch?
62645.e: The Napf is 1,408 m high and is the centre of a deeply cut hilly landscape.
62645.m: The Napf is the local mountain of the Emmental.

62646.q: What rock is most of the Napf upland made of?
62646.e: The Napf area is a large debris fan from the Molasse period; the cemented pebbles are called Nagelfluh.
62646.m: The Napf upland is mainly made of Nagelfluh.

62647.q: What are the typical ridges and narrow valleys in the Emmental called?
62647.e: Streams have cut deep into the soft Molasse rock; in between are narrow ridges, the Eggen, and tight valleys, the Gräben.
62647.m: The Emmental is a landscape of Eggen and Gräben.

62648.q: What is typical of the traditional Emmental farmhouse?
a: ground floor built of rubble stone
62648.e: The Emmental farmhouse combines living quarters, cowshed and barn under an enormous hipped or half-hipped roof that reaches far down.
62648.m: Emmental farmhouses have huge roofs that reach far down.

62649.q: Which doctor and politician from Nidau is considered the initiator of the Jura Water Correction?
62649.e: Johann Rudolf Schneider campaigned for decades to drain the Seeland, which suffered from floods.
62649.m: Johann Rudolf Schneider started the Jura Water Correction.

62650.q: Why has St Peter's Island no longer been a real island since the first Jura Water Correction?
a: It was filled up with earth.
62650.e: When Lake Biel was lowered by about two metres, a strip of land to Erlach appeared, the Heidenweg.
62650.m: The Heidenweg connects St Peter's Island with Erlach.

62651.q: Which town is the main town of the Seeland administrative district?
62651.e: The Seeland administrative district covers the rural part of the region; its seat is the small town of Aarberg.
62651.m: Aarberg is the main town of the Seeland administrative district.

62652.q: Which nickname is used for the Seeland with the Grosses Moos?
62652.e: A great many vegetables are grown on the drained marsh soils of the Grosses Moos.
62652.m: The Seeland is known as the vegetable garden of Switzerland.

62653.q: Why was a second Jura Water Correction needed between 1962 and 1973?
62653.e: After drainage, the peat soils of the Grosses Moos sank considerably, and floods happened again.
62653.m: The sinking of the peat soils made a second correction necessary.

62654.q: Which town is the largest bilingual town in Switzerland?
62654.e: In Biel/Bienne, German and French are used equally in everyday life and in the administration.
62654.m: Biel/Bienne is the largest bilingual town in Switzerland.

62655.q: Which philosopher lived on St Peter's Island in Lake Biel in 1765?
62655.e: Rousseau spent a few weeks on the island in 1765 and later described it as the happiest time of his life.
62655.m: Rousseau found refuge on St Peter's Island.

62656.q: Since which year have the prehistoric pile dwellings around the Alps, including in the Seeland, been a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
62656.e: The prehistoric pile dwellings around the Alps became World Heritage in 2011; several sites lie on the lakes of the Seeland.
62656.m: The pile dwellings have been UNESCO World Heritage since 2011.

62657.q: In which district of Upper Valais is Zermatt?
62657.e: Zermatt lies at the far end of the Matter Valley, a side valley of the Visp Valley, and belongs to the district of Visp.
62657.m: Zermatt belongs to the district of Visp.

62658.q: In which district of Upper Valais does the Rhône rise?
62658.e: The Rhône rises from the Rhône Glacier near Gletsch in the uppermost part of Goms.
62658.m: The Rhône begins in Goms at the Rhône Glacier.

62659.q: Which pass connects Brig with Domodossola in Italy?
62659.e: The Simplon road was built under Napoleon; the pass leads at 2,005 m from Upper Valais to Italy.
62659.m: The Simplon takes you from Brig to Domodossola.

62660.q: Which forest near the language border is considered one of the largest pine forests in the Alps?
62660.e: The Pfyn Forest between Leuk and Sierre lies in the border area between Upper and Lower Valais.
62660.m: The Pfyn Forest is a large pine forest in Valais.

62661.q: What status did Lower Valais have until 1798?
a: Subject territory of the Upper Valais Zenden
Part of the Duchy of Milan
Bailiwick of the canton of Bern
62661.e: After fighting with Savoy, the Zenden of upper Valais ruled Lower Valais from the late 15th century until the French invasion of 1798.
62661.m: Lower Valais was a subject territory until 1798.

62662.q: What were the seven territorial units of upper Valais called in the early modern period?
62662.e: The Republic of the Seven Zenden (Goms, Brig, Visp, Raron, Leuk, Sierre, Sion) was the centre of power of old Valais.
62662.m: Old Valais was divided into seven Zenden.

62663.q: Which pass connects Lower Valais with the Aosta Valley?
62663.e: The Great St Bernard leads from Martigny through the Val d'Entremont to Aosta; the famous hospice stands at the top of the pass.
62663.m: The Great St Bernard takes you from Lower Valais to Aosta.

62664.q: Near which town does the Rhône turn north in a striking bend?
62664.e: At Martigny, the Rhône turns from its westward course towards the north, heading for Lake Geneva.
62664.m: The Rhône makes its bend at Martigny.

62665.e: The Toggenburg is formed mainly by the valley of the Thur and the Neckertal.
62665.m: The Thur flows through the Toggenburg.

62666.q: Which place is considered the main town of the Toggenburg?
62666.e: Wattwil is the largest place and the centre of the valley. Wil already lies outside, in the Fürstenland.
62666.m: Wattwil is the main town of the Toggenburg.

62667.q: Which work did Ulrich Bräker from Wattwil write in the 18th century?
62667.e: Bräker (1735 to 1798) described his life as a small farmer and yarn trader; the book is an important autobiography from the lower classes.
62667.m: Ulrich Bräker told the story of the poor man of Toggenburg.

62668.q: Which mountain range forms the southern border of the Toggenburg and drops steeply to Lake Walen?
62668.e: The Churfirsten are the landmark of the Toggenburg; their south side plunges in steep cliffs to Lake Walen.
62668.m: The Churfirsten border the Toggenburg to the south.

62669.q: Which war broke out after the death of the last Count of Toggenburg in 1436?
62669.e: Count Frederick VII died in 1436 without a will; the dispute over his inheritance between Zurich and Schwyz led to the Old Zurich War.
62669.m: The death of the last Toggenburg count started the Old Zurich War.

62670.q: To whom was the Toggenburg sold in 1468?
62670.e: Petermann von Raron sold the Toggenburg to the Prince-Abbey of St Gallen for 14,500 guilders.
62670.m: From 1468 the Abbot of St Gallen ruled the Toggenburg.

62671.q: Which war of 1712 arose from a conflict over the Toggenburg?
62671.e: The dispute between the people of Toggenburg and the Abbot of St Gallen grew in 1712 into the Second War of Villmergen (Toggenburg War).
62671.m: The Toggenburg War of 1712 is also called the Second War of Villmergen.

62672.q: At 2,502 m, which mountain is the highest peak in the Toggenburg area?
62672.e: The Säntis in the Alpstein massif is 2,502 m high and clearly towers above the Churfirsten.
62672.m: The Säntis is the highest mountain by the Toggenburg.

62673.q: Which river flows through the Leventina?
62673.e: The Ticino rises in the Gotthard area and flows through the Leventina as far as Biasca.
62673.m: The Leventina is the valley of the Ticino.

62674.q: Between which places does the Leventina stretch?
62674.e: The valley reaches from the foot of the Gotthard Pass at Airolo to Biasca, where the Brenno flows in.
62674.m: The Leventina reaches from Airolo to Biasca.

62675.q: Which place is the main town of the Leventina?
62675.e: Faido is the main town of the Leventina district and was already the centre of the valley under the rule of Uri.
62675.m: Faido is the main town of the Leventina.

62676.q: Which canton ruled the Leventina as a subject territory until 1798?
62676.e: With its victory at the Battle of Giornico in 1478, Uri secured rule over the valley; it lasted until the end of the Old Swiss Confederacy in 1798.
62676.m: The Leventina was a subject territory of Uri until 1798.

62677.q: What happened in the Leventina in 1755?
a: the building of the Gotthard road
the founding of the canton of Ticino
62677.e: The Leventina uprising was directed against the rule of the bailiffs; it was bloodily put down, and three leaders were executed in Faido.
62677.m: In 1755 the Leventina uprising was bloodily put down.

62678.q: How does the old Gotthard railway overcome the steep steps in the Leventina?
62678.e: In the Piottino and Biaschina gorges, the railway gains height in circular spiral tunnels without the gradient becoming too steep.
62678.m: The Gotthard railway climbs through spiral tunnels in the Leventina.

62679.q: Near which place in the Leventina is the southern portal of the Gotthard Base Tunnel?
62679.e: The 57 km long Gotthard Base Tunnel runs from Erstfeld to Bodio.
62679.m: The Gotthard Base Tunnel ends in the south at Bodio.

62680.q: What is special about the Trümmelbach Falls in the Lauterbrunnen Valley?
62680.e: The Trümmelbach Falls are glacier waterfalls that have cut into the rock and can be visited inside the mountain; they drain the Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau.
62680.m: The Trümmelbach Falls thunder inside the mountain.

62681.q: On which peak is the revolving restaurant “Piz Gloria”, known from a James Bond film?
62681.e: “On Her Majesty's Secret Service” was filmed on the 2,970 m high Schilthorn in 1969.
62681.m: The Piz Gloria restaurant is on the Schilthorn.

62682.q: Roughly how high are the Staubbach Falls near Lauterbrunnen?
62682.e: The Staubbach Falls drop around 297 m freely over a rock face into the Lauterbrunnen Valley.
62682.m: The Staubbach Falls are almost 300 m high.

62683.q: Which pyramid-shaped mountain on Lake Thun has a staircase with over 11,000 steps?
62683.e: The Niesen stairway beside the funicular has 11,674 steps and is considered the longest staircase in the world.
62683.m: The longest staircase in the world leads up the Niesen.

62684.q: Since when has the Jungfrau-Aletsch region been a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
62684.e: The Swiss Alps Jungfrau-Aletsch were added to the World Heritage List in 2001 as the first natural heritage site in the Alps.
62684.m: Jungfrau-Aletsch has been World Heritage since 2001.

62685.q: Where is the Ballenberg Open-Air Museum?
62685.e: The museum is in Hofstetten near Brienz and shows over 100 historic buildings from all over Switzerland.
62685.m: The Ballenberg Open-Air Museum is near Brienz.

62686.q: At which waterfall near Meiringen does Arthur Conan Doyle let Sherlock Holmes seemingly die?
62686.e: In the story “The Final Problem”, Holmes and Moriarty plunge into the depths at the Reichenbach Falls.
62686.m: Sherlock Holmes fought at the Reichenbach Falls near Meiringen.

62687.q: Which cattle breed is named worldwide after a valley in the Bernese Oberland?
62687.e: Simmental cattle come from the Simmental and are now bred all over the world.
62687.m: Simmental cattle come from the Bernese Oberland.

62688.q: On which lake is the Italian exclave of Campione d'Italia?
62688.e: Campione lies on the eastern shore of Lake Lugano and is completely surrounded by Swiss territory and the lake.
62688.m: Campione d'Italia is on Lake Lugano.

62689.q: Why did Campione not belong to the territory of what later became Switzerland in the Middle Ages?
a: It was owned by a Milanese monastery.
It belonged to the Diocese of Chur.
It was part of the Duchy of Savoy.
It was a free imperial city.
62689.e: Toto of Campione left the village in 777 to the monastery of Sant'Ambrogio in Milan, which owned it until 1797.
62689.m: Campione belonged to the Milanese monastery of Sant'Ambrogio for a long time.

62690.q: What changed for Campione d'Italia on 1 January 2020?
a: It joined the EU customs territory.
It became a province of its own.
62690.e: Until the end of 2019, Campione was in the Swiss economic area; since 2020 it has belonged to the EU customs territory.
62690.m: Since 2020 Campione has been in the EU customs territory.

62691.q: How large is the municipal area of Campione d'Italia including the lake surface?
62691.e: Campione covers about 2.6 km², of which only just under 1 km² is land and the rest is lake.
62691.m: At around 2.6 km², Campione is very small.

62692.q: What were the “Maestri campionesi” known for?
62692.e: From the 12th to the 14th century, stonemasons, sculptors and architects from Campione worked on churches all over northern Italy.
62692.m: The Maestri campionesi were famous master builders.

62693.q: Which Ticino municipality did Switzerland once offer, unsuccessfully, in exchange for Campione?
62693.e: Ticino tried to acquire Campione in 1800 and in 1814/15 and offered Indemini in return, which however stayed with Ticino.
62693.m: An exchange of Campione for Indemini never happened.

62694.q: Which Italian region does Campione d'Italia belong to?
62694.e: Campione belongs to the province of Como in Lombardy.
62694.m: Politically, Campione d'Italia is in Lombardy.

62695.q: Why do many tourists go shopping in Samnaun?
a: Many goods there are duty-free and cheaper
There is no VAT on rents there
People pay in euros instead of francs there
All shops there are also open at night
62695.e: Samnaun has been a customs-free zone since 1892. Goods such as perfume, alcohol, tobacco or fuel are therefore often cheaper than in the rest of the country.
62695.m: In Samnaun you can shop duty-free.

62696.q: For what reason was Samnaun originally excluded from the Swiss customs territory?
a: There was no road over Swiss territory.
Until then the valley belonged to Austria.
The municipality was too small for a customs office.
A treaty with Italy required it.
62696.e: Samnaun could only be reached via Tyrol, so goods arrived in the valley with duty paid and were expensive. The duty-free status first applied until a road was built and was later extended.
62696.m: Samnaun became duty-free because it could only be reached via Austria.

62697.q: From which valley in the Grisons can you reach Samnaun on Swiss roads?
62697.e: The Samnaun road branches off at Vinadi in the Lower Engadine. It is narrow, so many people drive via the Austrian side.
62697.m: From Switzerland you reach Samnaun via the Lower Engadine.

62698.q: Which dialect is spoken in Samnaun today?
62698.e: Samnaun is the only Swiss municipality in the Bavarian dialect area; people speak a southern Bavarian Tyrolean.

62699.q: Which language was spoken in Samnaun until the 19th century?
62699.e: In the 19th century, the population gradually switched from the Romansh idiom Vallader to German.
62699.m: Samnaun was once a Romansh village.

62700.q: With which Austrian resort does Samnaun form the Silvretta Arena ski area?
62700.e: The Silvretta Arena connects Samnaun across the national border with Ischgl in the Paznaun valley.
62700.m: Samnaun and Ischgl share a ski area.

62701.q: Which technical innovation was used for the first time in Samnaun?
62701.e: Samnaun ran the world's first aerial cable car with two floors in each cabin.
62701.m: The first double-decker cable car ran in Samnaun.

62702.q: What is forbidden in the Swiss National Park?
a: Staying overnight at the Hotel Il Fuorn
62702.e: The National Park is a strict nature reserve. Nature should develop without human interference, so hunting, logging and mowing are forbidden. Visitors may, however, hike on the paths.
62702.m: In the National Park, nature can develop without human interference.

62703.q: Which tree species dominates the forest in the Swiss National Park?
62703.e: Mountain pines and dwarf mountain pines make up around 90 per cent of the trees. About a third of the park is forested.
62703.m: Mountain pines are the main trees in the National Park.

62704.q: Roughly how old are the fossils of Monte San Giorgio?
62704.e: The layers are about 245 to 230 million years old. That makes them older than most dinosaur finds.
62704.m: The fossils of Monte San Giorgio are around 240 million years old.

62705.q: Between the arms of which lake is Monte San Giorgio?
62705.e: The mountain lies in southern Ticino between the two southern arms of Lake Lugano. The area is close to the border with Italy.
62705.m: Monte San Giorgio is on Lake Lugano.

62706.q: Which reptile from Monte San Giorgio is named after the canton of Ticino?
62706.e: Ticinosuchus was a land-living reptile related to crocodiles. The name contains the Latin Ticinum for Ticino.
62706.m: Ticinosuchus has the canton of Ticino in its name.

62707.q: Where does the name of the marine reptile Ceresiosaurus come from?
62707.e: In Italian, Lake Lugano is called Lago Ceresio. So Ceresiosaurus is named after the lake where it was found.
62707.m: Ceresiosaurus is named after Lago Ceresio.

62708.q: Which Ticino architect designed the fossil museum in Meride that opened in 2012?
62708.e: Mario Botta rebuilt and extended the museum. It shows originals and replicas of the finds.
62708.m: Mario Botta designed the fossil museum in Meride.

62709.q: Why are the fossils of Monte San Giorgio so exceptionally well preserved?
62709.e: At the bottom of the basin the water had little oxygen, so hardly any scavengers or bacteria broke down the bodies. That is why complete skeletons were often preserved.
62709.m: Low-oxygen water protected the animal remains from decay.

62710.q: What is the main aim of a UNESCO biosphere reserve such as the one in Entlebuch?
a: To protect nature and do business sustainably at the same time
To leave nature completely without people
To build as many hotels as possible
62710.e: In a biosphere reserve, people should live and work, for example in farming, forestry or tourism. At the same time, valuable habitats such as moors are protected.
62710.m: A biosphere combines nature protection and sustainable use.

62711.q: Which habitat is especially typical of the UNESCO Biosphere Entlebuch?
62711.e: The Entlebuch has some of the largest and most numerous moorland landscapes in Switzerland. They are protected by national moorland protection.
62711.m: The Entlebuch Biosphere is rich in moorland landscapes.

62712.q: Which national label has the UNESCO Biosphere Entlebuch also held since 2008?
62712.e: Since 2008, the Entlebuch has also been a regional nature park of national importance. It therefore carries both a national and an international label.
62712.m: Since 2008 the Entlebuch Biosphere has also been a regional nature park.

62713.q: Which mountain with extensive limestone pavements lies in the UNESCO Biosphere Entlebuch?
62713.e: The Schrattenfluh is made of limestone that rainwater has dissolved into karren (grooves). The Napf and the Rigi, by contrast, consist mostly of Nagelfluh.
62713.m: The Schrattenfluh in the Entlebuch is a karst landscape.

62714.q: In which year did Swiss voters accept the Rothenthurm initiative to protect moors?
62714.e: The initiative was accepted on 6 December 1987. Since then, moors of national importance have been protected in the Federal Constitution.
62714.m: The Rothenthurm initiative was accepted in 1987.

62716.q: Which building project in the Rothenthurm moor triggered the moorland protection initiative?
62716.e: The army wanted to build a training ground in the largest raised bog in Switzerland. Those affected then launched the initiative with the support of WWF.
62716.m: A planned army training ground led to the Rothenthurm initiative.

62717.q: According to the Federal Constitution, what is basically forbidden in moors of national importance?
a: New installations and changes to the ground
62717.e: Since the Rothenthurm initiative, no installations may be built and no changes to the ground made in protected moors. Gentle use is still possible.
62717.m: In protected moors, building is basically not allowed.

62718.q: Where does a true raised bog get its water from?
62718.e: A raised bog grows above the groundwater level and is fed only by rain. It is therefore poor in nutrients and acidic.
62718.m: Raised bogs are fed only by rainwater.

62719.q: Which genus of moss mainly builds up raised bogs?
62719.e: Peat mosses keep growing at the top and die off at the bottom. They store a lot of water and make their surroundings acidic.
62719.m: Peat mosses build up raised bogs.

62720.q: By how much does the peat layer of an intact raised bog grow per year on average?
62720.e: Peat grows only about one millimetre a year. One metre of peat therefore takes around 1,000 years.
62720.m: Peat grows only about one millimetre a year.

62721.q: Which type of moor is also fed by mineral-rich groundwater or slope water?
62721.e: Fens are within reach of groundwater, spring water or slope water and are richer in nutrients than raised bogs. Switzerland has its own inventory of fens.
62721.m: Fens get water from the ground or from the slope.

62722.q: Why are there far fewer moors in Switzerland today than around 1800?
a: They were drained and dug for peat
They dried out because of earthquakes
62722.e: Over 80 per cent of the moorland was lost. People drained it for farming and settlements and cut peat as fuel.
62722.m: Most of Switzerland's moors were drained or dug for peat.

62723.q: Roughly how many sites does the Federal Inventory of Landscapes and Natural Monuments (BLN) include?
62723.e: The BLN includes 162 sites, from small natural monuments to large mountain landscapes. Together they cover around a fifth of Switzerland.
62723.m: The BLN inventory includes around 160 sites.

62724.q: What share of Switzerland's land area do the BLN sites cover together?
62724.e: Together, the 162 sites cover about 19 per cent of the country's area. They range from small natural monuments to large mountain landscapes.
62724.m: The BLN sites cover around a fifth of Switzerland.

62725.q: Which federal law is the BLN inventory based on?
a: Nature and Cultural Heritage Protection Act
62725.e: The BLN is based on Article 5 of the Nature and Cultural Heritage Protection Act (NHG). It came into force on 1 July 1966.
62725.m: The BLN is based on the Nature and Cultural Heritage Protection Act.

62726.q: What does the federal BLN inventory mainly protect?
62726.e: The BLN lists landscapes and natural monuments of national importance. There are separate federal inventories for townscapes and historic traffic routes (ISOS and IVS).
62726.m: The BLN protects landscapes and natural monuments of national importance.

62727.q: Who drew up the earlier inventory on which the BLN is based?
a: Private nature and heritage protection associations
62727.e: Pro Natura, the Heritage Society and the Swiss Alpine Club created the private KLN inventory from 1959 to 1963. The Confederation later took it over as the basis for the BLN.
62727.m: The BLN goes back to an inventory by private protection associations.

62728.q: For whom is the BLN inventory directly binding?
a: For federal offices carrying out federal tasks
62728.e: The BLN binds the Confederation, for example when granting permits, concessions or subsidies. It has no direct legal effect on landowners.
62728.m: The BLN inventory mainly obliges the Confederation.

62729.q: What does the NHG basically require for BLN sites when federal tasks are carried out?
62729.e: Under Article 6 NHG, BLN sites should be preserved undiminished or at least spared as much as possible. Exceptions are only possible for equal or greater interests of national importance.
62729.m: BLN sites should be preserved as undiminished as possible.

62730.q: Which object typically counts as a natural monument in the BLN?
62730.e: Natural monuments in the BLN include erratic boulders, rock outcrops and other geotopes. Buildings such as castles belong in other inventories.
62730.m: An erratic boulder can be protected as a natural monument in the BLN.

62731.q: Which three categories of parks of national importance does Swiss law recognise?
a: National park, regional nature park, nature discovery park
National park, city park, amusement park
Wildlife park, animal park, bird park
Nature park, forest park, lake park
62731.e: These three categories have existed since the Parks Ordinance of 2007. Regions can apply to the Confederation for the corresponding park label.
62731.m: Switzerland has national parks, regional nature parks and nature discovery parks.

62732.q: What characterises a nature discovery park under Swiss law?
a: Core zone close to a built-up area
62732.e: A nature discovery park lies no more than about 20 km from a densely populated area. In its core zone nature should develop freely, and a transition zone is for experiencing nature.
62732.m: A nature discovery park offers wilderness close to the city.

62733.q: Which park was recognised as Switzerland's first nature discovery park?
62733.e: The Sihlwald south of Zurich was the first park to receive the nature discovery park label. In its core zone, the beech forest is no longer used.
62733.m: The Sihlwald was Switzerland's first nature discovery park.

62734.q: Roughly between which towns does Lavaux stretch?
62734.e: The vineyard terraces stretch along the northern shore of Lake Geneva from Lausanne to the area around Vevey. They are among the most impressive wine landscapes in Switzerland.
62734.m: Lavaux lies between Lausanne and Vevey.

62735.q: Which vineyard site in Lavaux is one of the two Grand Cru sites?
62735.e: Dézaley and Calamin are the two Grand Cru sites of Lavaux. Salgesch, Twann and Fläsch are wine-growing villages in other regions.
62735.m: Dézaley is a Grand Cru site in Lavaux.

62736.q: From which century were the steep vineyard terraces in Lavaux built?
62736.e: The terraces were built from the 12th century onwards, partly at the suggestion of monasteries. They are still supported by dry stone walls today.
62736.m: The vineyard terraces in Lavaux were built from the 12th century.

62737.q: Which environmentalist launched a popular initiative in 1977 to save Lavaux?
62737.e: Franz Weber's initiative led in 1977 to a protection article in the constitution of the canton of Vaud. Weber remained a leading campaigner for the landscape until his death.
62737.m: Franz Weber campaigned for the protection of Lavaux in 1977.

62738.q: How long is the surveyed cave system of the Hölloch (as of 2022)?
62738.e: By November 2022, 210.229 km of passages had been surveyed. Research is still going on.
62738.m: The Hölloch is over 210 kilometres long.

62739.q: In which valley in the canton of Schwyz is the Hölloch?
62739.e: The entrance to the Hölloch is near Stalden in the Muotatal in the canton of Schwyz. The cave system stretches far beneath the karst area of the Silberen.
62739.m: The Hölloch is in the Muotatal.

62740.q: Who was the first to go deep into the Hölloch in 1875?
62740.e: Alois Ulrich, a mountain farmer from Stalden, began exploring in 1875. Systematic research started in 1889.
62740.m: Alois Ulrich explored the Hölloch from 1875.

62741.q: How were the passages of the Hölloch mainly formed?
a: Limestone dissolved by water containing carbonic acid
62741.e: Water containing carbonic acid dissolves limestone chemically. Over a long time, this karst process created the passages and halls.
62741.m: Water containing carbonic acid hollowed out the Hölloch in limestone.

62742.q: Roughly how big is the difference in height within the Hölloch?
62742.e: The difference in height between the lowest and highest point is 1,033 m. The passages mostly slope down towards the north.
62742.m: The Hölloch has a height difference of around 1,000 metres.

62743.q: Why can most of the lowest level of the Hölloch not be entered?
a: It lies below the karst water table
62743.e: The system has roughly three levels. The lowest mostly lies below the karst water table and is filled with water.
62743.m: The deepest level of the Hölloch is under water.

62744.q: Which danger can trap researchers in the Hölloch for days?
62744.e: After heavy rain, the water rises quickly and blocks passages. Researchers have been trapped for several days until the water went down again.
62744.m: Flooding is the biggest danger in the Hölloch.

62745.q: Roughly how far do the rock walls of the Creux du Van drop vertically?
62745.e: The limestone cliffs drop around 160 m vertically. The basin is about 1,200 m wide and 500 m deep.
62745.m: The rock walls of the Creux du Van are around 160 metres high.

62746.q: How long is the rock amphitheatre of the Creux du Van altogether?
62746.e: The cliffs form a semicircle around 4 km long. They are a well-known landmark of the Jura.
62746.m: The rock amphitheatre of the Creux du Van is around four kilometres long.

62747.q: According to current thinking, how was the rock basin of the Creux du Van probably formed?
a: By erosion after the Würm glacial period
As the crater of a volcano
62747.e: The basin was probably shaped by erosion after the last glacial period. Frost and water wore away the rock.
62747.m: Erosion after the last ice age shaped the Creux du Van.

62748.q: What is special about the Fontaine Froide spring in the Creux du Van?
a: Water at around 4 °C all year round
62748.e: The spring lies in the shady basin and carries water at a steady temperature of about 4 °C all year. That is where its name “cold fountain” comes from.
62748.m: The Fontaine Froide always gives very cold water.

62749.q: Which predator was released in the Creux du Van area in 1974 and 1975?
62749.e: One pair of lynx each from the Slovakian Carpathians was released. The aim was to bring the lynx back to the Jura.
62749.m: Lynx were released in the Creux du Van in the 1970s.

62750.q: Since which year has the Creux du Van area been protected?
62750.e: The area was put under protection in 1972. It also belongs to the Federal Inventory of Landscapes of National Importance.
62750.m: The Creux du Van has been protected since 1972.

62751.q: How much of Switzerland's dry meadows and pastures has been lost since 1900?
62751.e: According to the Federal Office for the Environment, more than 95 per cent of these habitats have been destroyed since 1900. Their area and quality continue to decline.
62751.m: Over 95 per cent of dry meadows have disappeared since 1900.

62752.q: In which year did the Federal Council bring into force the inventory of dry meadows and pastures of national importance?
62752.e: In 2010, the Federal Council included the most valuable areas in a federal inventory under Article 18a NHG. The cantons put the protection into practice.
62752.m: The dry meadows inventory has existed since 2010.

62753.q: How does a dry pasture differ from a dry meadow?
a: It is grazed instead of mown
It is always in a forest
62753.e: Dry meadows are mown; dry pastures are grazed by livestock such as sheep or cattle. Both uses stop bushes from growing.
62753.m: A dry pasture is grazed, a dry meadow is mown.

62754.q: On which type of slope are dry meadows found especially often in the Alps?
62754.e: South-facing slopes get a lot of sun and dry out quickly. Plants that love warmth and resist drought thrive on their shallow soils.
62754.m: Dry meadows are often on sunny south-facing slopes.

62755.e: On shallow, often chalky and permeable soils, rainwater drains away quickly. Nutrients are scarce, so tall grasses can hardly take hold.
62755.m: Dry meadows grow on poor, permeable soils.

62756.q: Which two developments mainly threaten dry meadows in Switzerland?
62756.e: If the land is fertilised, fast-growing grasses push out the specialists. If use is abandoned, bushes and forest grow in.
62756.m: Fertilising and scrub encroachment destroy dry meadows.

62757.q: Which management best preserves a species-rich dry meadow?
62757.e: A late cut lets plants set seed and insects complete their development. Without fertiliser, the less competitive species survive.
62757.m: Dry meadows need late mowing and no fertiliser.

62758.q: Why are dry meadows especially rich in species?
a: Few nutrients stop a few species from taking over
They are heavily fertilised and grow fast
They are sown again every year
They are always in damp valleys
62758.e: On poor soils, fast-growing grasses cannot dominate. That leaves room for many specialised plants such as orchids, and with them many insects.
62758.m: Poor soils allow great species diversity.

62759.q: How does the forest line differ from the tree line?
a: Above the forest line there are only single trees
The tree line is always lower
The forest line only applies to broadleaved trees
62759.e: The forest line marks the end of closed forest. Above it, up to the tree line, there are only single trees or groups of trees.
62759.m: Above the forest line only single trees grow.

62760.q: Where is the natural forest line highest in Switzerland?
62760.e: In inner Alpine areas such as Valais and the Engadine, the forest reaches about 2,300 m, in the Northern Alps only around 1,800 m. The reason is the more continental, sunnier climate.
62760.m: In the Central Alps the forest climbs highest.

62761.q: What is the effect called by which large mountain massifs raise the forest line?
